purpose: Generate B2c publication and final composition under F-S06/F-S19. Replace both publishRetainedInScope and publishUniqueInScope seams with complete protected publication; remove SOURCE_EFFECTS_INCOMPLETE and every fabrication-incomplete seam. Preserve all reviewed host, read, reconstruction, semantic closure and physical synchronization effects. Inputs must be fully descriptor-safe admitted before mutation; retained entries canonicalized, exact text sorted/deduplicated, bounded as a whole, verified using shared witness/artifact laws, hashed with one LF per line. Unique full record is admitted and validated through existing Code addressUniqueJournalCommand/parseUniqueJournalRecord, never a Systems slot hash reimplementation. Resolve existing batch/occupied slot from current protected view without duplicate capacity charge or mutation; return original occupied entry. An existing retained batch can use the shared existing-file barrier to establish durable retention without republishing; unique occupancy remains an internal custody result whose full closure barrier belongs to the trusted domain caller. For new publication preflight source-file count, total physical bytes, and names-only discovery work (including new directories and final name) before source mutation. Extend private scanner/view accounting as necessary, retaining one authoritative scanner rather than adding another. New exact namespace directories may be created mode0700 with held and checked parent provenance; use no caller path components. Recheck operation bindings and held parents immediately before the existing writeFileAtomicNew durable create-only helper. Set operation.markPublicationPossible before entering helper, retain visible bytes, and keep conservative uncertainty through outer cleanup. Refresh state.view after publication; calculate ordinal unique root-wide newly retained and newly admitted event IDs from actual before/after state, preserving membership-only distinction and pending state. Unexpected occupancy must use verified original occupied resolution and can never be created; a helper failure that does not independently establish nonpublication remains uncertain. Public scope and owner keys stay exact. Do not add public authorization routes or claim domain admission; trusted domain composition still supplies authority and full closure barriers. Return one complete unaccepted source-patchset eligible for independent receiving after public source review. No production promotion or license choice.

contracts.selectedText:
**F-S01 — Source boundary.** Follow L-F01–L-F07 and F-P01–F-P06. The exact source root is the existing computer-system-engine package, bound by the generation inventory. Create only `src/journal/filesystem/source-owner.mjs` and `src/journal/diagnostics.mjs`; edit only `package.json` to add `./journal/filesystem/source-owner` and `./journal/diagnostics` exports to those paths. Preserve all existing package fields and exports. No dependency additions, operational data writes by the generator, new framework, alternate codec, permanent index, sidecar authority or Code-to-System import. The inventory binds the package bytes and absent targets before invocation. Read-only source inputs provide existing laws, not authority to preserve old storage machinery.


**F-S04 — Source discovery and verified views.** Apply the exact discovery grammar in F-S10. Bound directory iteration before accumulating entries, file lengths before allocating/read/parse, individual retained lines before parsing, complete physical scan bytes and distinct physical source count. Open recognized sources without following symlinks, verify descriptor and named bindings and lengths before/after the bounded read. Parse UTF-8 strictly with the shared codec. Retained batches require filename SHA-256 of exact bytes, canonical nonempty sorted/deduplicated JSONL entries and final LF; unique files require the exact canonical verified whole record plus LF. Reject wrong-address, malformed, conflicting or unrecognized custody rather than claiming a successful empty source view. Enforce the fixed unique envelope separately from retained-container L-O23 capacity.

Discover unique sources into the same causal/artifact view, including L-O26's addressed command body and virtual feed using the original observation's date and subject. Keep original verified witness values for custody separately from normalized query envelopes. Use L-O27's normalized-envelope conflict rule. Collect historical obstruction decisions before rebuilding; preserve falsy values and bodyless blocks. Apply L-O25's exact-source derived-view reuse: unchanged parsed source entries need not repeat artifact verification, monotone additions use receiveSourceSet for previously unseen bodies, and withdrawal/replacement/changed decisions rebuild from complete verified current input. Every operation still reads/hashes the bounded source set, and no cache suppresses corruption or discovery.


**F-S05 — Reads, selections and measurement.** Implement the closed scope result and argument shapes exactly. Runtime JS arguments must be descriptor-safe finite snapshots under their applicable existing envelope; do not invoke accessors as part of argument admission. Verify dense arrays, ordinality, reference syntax and closed selection fields without coercion. Invalid programmer arguments throw TypeError without source mutation; required-but-absent evidence yields the declared storage diagnostic. L-O24 governs exact feed/date/territory/as-of semantics. Establish complete selected admission before returning envelopes to a fold; preserve core-only and bodyless-block distinctions in exact witness observations. As-of validates required full-root causal closure before intersecting feed memberships. Use existing topological order with ordinal identity ties. Feed completeness does not require an unrelated pending feed to be ready. Source status and physical usage remain separate exact L-M measurements, with deeply immutable return values. The owner grants no public disclosure authority.


**F-S06 — Publication under the held gate.** Validate a proposed retained batch or unique record completely before mutation, including canonical source bytes, feed safety, declared reference/body correspondence and source/scan capacity for a genuinely new source. A known byte-identical batch or occupied unique slot does not consume a second source-file quota. Sort/deduplicate retained entry text before hashing; never silently split or truncate a batch. Preserve the distinction between newly retained event IDs, newly admitted event IDs and membership-only changes. Publish using only the existing durable create-only primitive, then refresh the same protected view. An existing unique slot is parsed and returned as the original occupied entry; never overwrite it with the proposed command or return created on recovery.

Verify the parent bindings before publication and reject symlink/nondirectory source parents. Missing exact source namespace directories may be created with mode 0700 while holding the gate, using no path component from a caller except an already admitted feed stored as metadata. No physical dated feed is written. A failure after entering create-only publication is conservatively publication-uncertain unless nonpublication is established independently; the helper has no stage marker. Preflight capacity/argument failures remain their proper nonpublication outcome. Visible bytes are preserved. A retained pending witness is not an admitted-closure acknowledgment. InitializeJournal also synchronizes host, stable lock and ancestors, checks existing identity-bearing unique custody, preserves a differing existing host and returns created only after its successful live publication barrier.


**F-S07 — Required evidence and existing-source durability.** Implement L-O26–L-O28's closure, longest causal path, exact semantic byte charges, sufficient physical custody cover and opaque per-scope barrier evidence. Source synchronization must use the same verified descriptors, include mandatory original unique occupancy, and synchronize required directory entries bottom-up through the filesystem root. Bind every name and ancestor; do not assume O_NOFOLLOW on the final file validates its parent path. Recheck required bytes even on cache hits. A successful existing-source barrier neither republishes evidence nor creates staging files, and common duplicate site bodies must not force synchronization of unrelated history. Do not add an alternate closure codec, interpret arbitrary embedded strings as edges, or require fabricated envelopes for core-only causal evidence.


**F-S08 — Independent receiving responsibility.** The source provider returns a candidate from this public contract and exact supplied bytes, with no tool access and no private receiving material. It is not asked to execute or certify future acceptance. Refuse only for a specific missing/contradictory source requirement or inability to supply the implementation, not because the intentionally isolated provider cannot run the assessor. The independent operator commits private fixtures before generation, materializes the closed patchset, syntax-checks the staged files and runs it in a network-denied namespace with only required dependencies and fixture directories. No credentials or operational corpus enter receiving. Review source for binding/descriptor cleanup, budget enforcement, gate lifetime, private diagnostic leakage, uncertainty handling and custody correspondence even if fixtures pass. No assessor behavioral repair or private-feedback retry is permitted.

Receiving must demonstrate initialization/retry/conflict, unchanged identities across reopen, same-process and separate-process exclusion, scope expiry and callback error preservation, ordinary/unique shared discovery, original command-payload recovery, duplicate/conflicting requests, pending-to-admitted recovery, retained blocks, membership-only additions, exact selections and accounting, source withdrawal/corruption, changed root/host/lock refusal, configured resource refusals and actual required-source synchronization with failure injection. Further integration receiving must establish all L-O06 consumer effects and legacy retirement before the replacement is called complete. A finite fixture set alone does not prove all host/production properties.


**F-S09 — Evidence and promotion boundary.** Record the exact specification/dependency/input/assay/candidate digests, requested and observed Luna model, executable/profile, namespace observation, invocation duration, measured tokens, and cash cost unavailable when not reported. The generation inventory and public source bundle are immutable during an invocation. Any unexpected provider tool activity or source change rejects it. A passing owner candidate remains a dependency, not an accepted operating application. Before any promotion recheck all protected bytes and absent targets and preserve exact originals; report partial multi-file promotion honestly. Do not remove the old writer or mutate a real journal in this dependency order. The connected facade/domain/consumer and offline migration patchset carries the retirement obligation.


**F-S10 — Closed source namespace and bounded discovery.** The runtime recognizes root host.json and maintenance.lock, optional retained/v1 and unique-admissions/v1 directory chains, and their exact source filenames. In retained/v1 a final filename is 64 lowercase hexadecimal digits plus `.jsonl`; in unique-admissions/v1 it is 64 lowercase hexadecimal digits plus `.json`. A staging sibling is exactly an admitted final basename followed by a dot, one or more ASCII decimal PID digits, a dot, a lowercase hexadecimal UUID in 8-4-4-4-12 groups, and `.tmp`. At the root, host.json may have this same staging suffix. Verify staging entries are regular nonsymlink files; exclude their bodies from source semantics and source-file/source-byte totals, never treat them as complete publications, and do not delete them. Arbitrary `.tmp` names are not exempt. The accepted helper's same-directory staging is outside the recognized *final filename* namespace, not necessarily outside its physical directory.

Stream directory entries with bounded work. Charge each encountered entry's root-relative UTF-8 path bytes plus one separator unit to a separate discovery-work counter capped by configured maxScanBytes. This derives a finite discovery bound from existing host capacity without changing the independent physical-source byte total. Include directories, host/lock, staging names and rejected entries in this work counter; increment and check before saving metadata or descending. Use overflow-safe remaining-capacity comparisons. Source-file and exact file-byte limits continue to apply only to final source files, deduplicated by physical identity. Do not load an unbounded readdir array first. No symlink or special file is followed. Unexpected versions, names or nested entries inside recognized source families are source-corrupt; unexpected root custody is storage-unavailable with a private namespace/migration distinction, never ignored successful emptiness.

Runtime must refuse known old custody: root compaction.jsonl; index/causal-admission/v1 or v2, including compacting.lock; objects/sen/sha-256; feed-relative `.statements` or `.index` custody trees; and `.witnesses` segments. Feed handles need not have a `.jsonl` extension. Plain directory names index/objects are not themselves proof of legacy custody. Their presence is nevertheless outside this runtime's closed source namespace and cannot be silently interpreted as disposable. A dated directory or other unknown old layout likewise prevents claiming the new root is complete until offline migration has accounted for it. Do not recursively parse or repair old formats at runtime. Known-source markers inform the private migration-required diagnostic; an unknown layout is a private unrecognized-root-custody diagnostic with the same storage-unavailable public reason.

Explicit initialization may provision an old ordinary-custody root for later offline migration as L-H05 permits; that does not make runtime opening succeed. It must still boundedly discover any existing new unique source family and verify every record under the proposed journal identity before creating host.json. Conflicting or uninterpretable identity-bearing custody refuses before host publication. No new migration receipt schema or special ignored metadata directory is invented by this dependency order. A root containing a purported receipt whose identity/format is not admitted remains unavailable until the separate migration contract accounts for it. Empty directories, old files and staging leftovers are not automatically removed by either API.


**F-S11 — Two dependent source-generation stages.** The complete owner may be generated in two source calls after the first whole-owner provider declined to supply an implementation. This changes the source-call boundary, not the required final behavior, private receiving fixtures, source inventory or promotion condition. Both stages remain unaccepted outside the working repository until the combined result satisfies the complete order. The operator does not write or repair product behavior.

Stage A supplies the complete diagnostics module, package exports, explicit host initialization, immutable root/host binding, descriptor-owned gate and withOperation lifetime/error handling. Within source-owner.mjs it leaves exactly one designated private generation seam:

```js
function createSourceScope(operation) {
  throw new TypeError("journal source view fabrication incomplete");
}
```

This seam is an explicit staging-only incompleteness marker, never a runtime fallback and never promotable. withOperation calls it under the held gate before invoking the trusted callback. Its operation argument is a frozen private object containing exactly root (bound absolute directory), configuration (the deeply frozen admitted host configuration), cache (one owner-private mutable cell with property value, initially undefined), assertLive (throws outside this operation), assertBindings (rechecks current root/host/lock bindings), and markPublicationPossible (sets the operation's uncertainty flag irreversibly). Methods check the captured lifetime, not a caller-supplied flag. The argument is never returned or serialized. The host stage provides all actual initialization and host-boundary behavior; it does not pretend a source view exists.

Stage B receives the exact generated Stage-A bytes and the source-view specification/dependencies. It replaces that private seam with the complete source reader, scope methods, source-derived cache, publication and durability behavior; additional private helpers may be inserted within the same owner module. It may refine Stage-A private helper composition where necessary while preserving all host and diagnostic contracts. It removes the staging-only error and all placeholders. No public alternate constructor or partially functional scope survives. The final inventory retains the original checkout package digest and absent creation targets for eventual promotion; Stage-B staging edits are bound separately to the precise Stage-A source bytes.

Syntax and public source review may occur between stages; the complete committed private receiver runs only against the composed result after Stage B. Source-provider input includes only the clauses and dependency source needed for its stage, with hashes binding the full order and predecessor files. Private receiving outcomes are never sent to either provider. A refusal or failure preserves the incomplete stages as unaccepted evidence and does not authorize hand completion or a reduced acceptance claim.


**F-S15 — Separate source reconstruction from scope effects.** Stage-B attempt05 declined the remaining complete implementation even with the existing address API explicitly supplied. Split that unfinished source work into B1 and B2; this supersedes only F-S11's Stage-B invocation boundary. The final source inventory, required behavior and independent receiver remain unchanged. No intermediate phase is promoted or assessed as a working owner. All stages are generated in isolated fresh contexts; the operator supplies specifications and deterministic staging, never behavioral repairs.

B1 generates the bounded recognized-source discovery and verified derived view only. Add private `refreshSourceView(operation)` and its necessary private helpers to the staged source-owner.mjs. Keep the exact createSourceScope incompleteness seam and all existing host code unchanged except imports needed by B1. B1 is not responsible for resolving F-S13's existing host defects: B2 must correct them before complete receiving. Do not generate public scope methods, publication or fsync/barrier behavior in B1. The ordinary and unique source reader must itself satisfy F-S04/F-S10, L-O22/L-O23/L-O25/L-O26/L-O27's source-correspondence rule, and the existing wire/causal laws. Existing filesystem helper use remains in the host code; B1 performs bounded reads and derived-memory construction only.

`operation` is exactly the F-S11 private context. Call operation.assertLive and operation.assertBindings before reading and after reconstruction. The value returned by refreshSourceView is an internal record, never returned to a user or serialized. Its fields are:

| Field | Internal representation and meaning |
| --- | --- |
| substrate | The existing Code CausalSubstrate instance, obtained by unwrapping a successful rebuildCausalSubstrate/receiveSourceSet judgment |
| sources | Map from recognized root-relative final filename to `{name,kind,identity,size,digest,bytes,parsed}`; name is that key, kind is `retained` or `unique`, identity is frozen `{dev,ino}`, size is exact byte length, digest is SHA-256 of exact bytes, bytes is the private bounded Buffer, and parsed is the verified retained-entry array or parseUniqueJournalRecord result |
| envelopes | Map from event reference to `{statement,canonicalText}`, the normalized verified envelope and its canonical text; retain original verified values inside source parsed records |
| feedEvents | Map from admitted safe-feed string to Set of retained event references with that membership, regardless of current causal state |
| artifactCustody | Map from verified artifact reference to Set of recognized source names containing its exact body or L-O26's verified embedded command body |
| envelopeCustody | Map from event reference to Set of recognized source names containing its agreed normalized envelope |
| uniqueEntries | Map from slot digest to the authoritative parseUniqueJournalRecord result; a copied ordinary witness/body never supplies this map |
| historicalObstructions | Map from event reference to canonical-text-sorted, exact-deduplicated arrays of original verified retained obstruction JSON values, including falsy values and bodyless events |
| sourceFiles | Distinct recognized physical-source count under L-M03 |
| sourceBytes | Sum of exact lengths of those distinct physical sources under L-M03 |

The maps and Buffer are private derived state. They must not escape through future scope results; B2 copies/freezes public values according to L-O02. No method mutates the substrate's internal maps. The cache cell belongs to the owner. It may contain a private state record with the last complete view and the metadata necessary for L-O25's reuse. B1 installs a replacement cache value only after discovery/verification/reconstruction and final binding checks succeed. A partially processed source set is never installed as the current view. If mutable substrate receiveSourceSet would be used for a monotone update, ensure all new source records and correspondence/decision checks have passed before delivering the complete set of unseen bodies; invalidate the cache if a later failure leaves its derived judgment unsuitable for reuse. Do not build and discard a second complete substrate merely to claim warm reuse.

Discovery streams the root and exact source-family directories under F-S10. It rejects an unsupported root layout or corrupted recognized family rather than ignoring it. Bound current descriptor lengths and reads before allocation, close descriptors without masking the primary failure, bind nonsymlink parents and final names before/after reads, and enforce all corpus/discovery limits. Unique whole-record bytes retain the fixed JSON envelope; retained entries use L-O23's line-derived envelope, while their artifact bodies and obstruction values retain their own smaller envelopes. Parsing canonical source bytes must compare the actual bytes to the required representation, not compare two normalized values. Retained batches require exact canonical sorted/deduplicated entry lines, LF, and filename/body digest agreement. A unique source requires canonical verified record plus LF and filename slot correspondence through the existing parser. No source read calls create-only publication or creates a missing directory.

For source mapping, verify each ordinary statement with parseJournalWitness, register its original source pairs as artifact custody, register its normalized envelope and feed membership, and detect normalized-envelope conflicts by event reference. Register standalone retained artifacts only after the existing artifact verifier succeeds. Collect historical decisions from retained obstruction entries before causal reconstruction, retaining exact original values. Unique records register their witness source pairs, explicit record artifacts, L-O26's addressed parsed command body, normalized envelope and F-S14's virtual feed. Duplicate body references must agree in canonical text; duplicate envelope references must agree in normalized canonical text. Duplicate physical custody must not inflate semantic counts or replace an original unique record.

On a cold view call rebuildCausalSubstrate with the complete unique verified source pairs and all current retained obstruction records in its fourth argument. Use the returned substrate, including its admission, quarantine and obstruction judgments; a retained blocked decision is not an owner-invented second evaluator. On a warm view, exact physical identities/digests and decisions establish the unchanged, monotone-addition or rebuild case in L-O25. Build membership and custody maps from every current record even when parsed/semantic verification is reused. A removed source invalidates its custody and unique occupancy contribution. A malformed changed source refuses; it does not behave like removal. Return private fields with the exact above meanings, leaving sourceStatus, events and the remaining public scope assembly to B2.

B2 receives the exact staged B1 bytes, the complete owner contracts and public F-S13 corrections. It replaces createSourceScope with the complete scope API using refreshSourceView, supplies protected publication and closure/barrier methods, completes host corrections, and removes every incompleteness marker. It may refactor B1's private representation only if every consumer is changed coherently in the same generated candidate; no obsolete adapter survives. Only this composed result is eligible for the unchanged complete receiver and final source review. Finishing B1 is source-generation progress, not storage or assistant acceptance.


**F-S19 — Generate remaining operations in dependency order.** Attempt14 supplied no B2 implementation. Decompose B2 into B2a (read scope), B2b (required-evidence barrier and host corrections), and B2c (publication and final composition). This changes only the invocation boundary. The complete owner contract, writable inventory, final independent receiver and connected migration/retirement obligations remain unchanged. Do not interpret a partial stage as a usable or accepted owner. Generate all behavioral source in isolated contexts from the existing specifications and exact preceding staged bytes.

B2a replaces createSourceScope's single incompleteness seam with the live, frozen read scope. Implement witness, artifact, feeds, events, sourceStatus, sourceUsage and uniqueRecord under L-O01/L-O02/L-O05/L-O22/L-O24/L-M01–L-M03. Use the complete existing refreshSourceView and the existing Code topological/causal laws. Complete read selections before exposing any envelopes, preserve core-only and bodyless-block observations, and enforce full-root required causal readiness for as-of before feed intersection. Preserve exact root-relative feed/date/frontier laws and descriptor-safe closed input admission. Do not add a second source scanner, causal evaluator or writable lookup. Public scope fields are exactly the ten methods: witness, artifact, feeds, events, sourceStatus, sourceUsage, uniqueRecord, publishRetained, publishUnique, requireDurable. The owner itself still exposes only withOperation.

For dependent composition, createSourceScope constructs private state `{operation,view}` where operation is the existing F-S11 context and view is the current refreshSourceView result. Brand the scope privately and retain this state only inside owner-private closures/WeakMap; no state/view/refresh method is public. All methods check the captured operation lifetime. Read methods use the current state.view, not a stale lexical copy; later publication must replace it with the refreshed complete view. Internal helper names may be chosen by generation, but B2a must define the three exact effect boundaries `publishRetainedInScope(state, entries)`, `publishUniqueInScope(state, record)` and `requireDurableInScope(state, requirement)`. Each has only the explicit incompleteness behavior of throwing TypeError with the fixed message `journal source effects fabrication incomplete`. The scope's corresponding methods perform the lifetime check and delegate to these private boundaries. These deliberate temporary seams are forbidden in final B2c. They supply no publication, durability or authorization success.

B2a preserves existing host functions and the reviewed physical/reconstruction paths except necessary imports and coherent private scope integration. F-S13 host corrections remain explicitly assigned to B2b; B2a does not claim them complete. Read results are deeply immutable and carry the exact prescribed shapes, with canonical body text retained as encoded document text rather than admitted again as one artifact string. Do not impose an artifact envelope on a retained normalized witness container; use its already verified source-derived value or the admitted line capacity when a snapshot is required. Internal source failures retain the closed diagnostic boundary, while malformed programmer input throws TypeError before mutation. No complete receiver runs against the deliberate seams.

B2b receives the exact staged B2a bytes. Replace requireDurableInScope with all L-O04/L-O26–L-O28 closure, longest causal path, exact witness/artifact charges, sufficient physical custody selection and existing-descriptor/ancestor barriers. Bind opaque receipts privately to the captured scope epoch and exact closure. Implement F-S13 host/init/cleanup/uncertainty corrections, using the same bound-descriptor barrier for initializeJournal's verified host/lock and ancestor custody. Preserve both publication seams and all read effects. It remains unaccepted and is not run through the complete receiver while those seams exist.

B2c receives that exact staged result. Implement publishRetainedInScope and publishUniqueInScope under L-O03/L-O05/F-S06, including descriptor-safe complete preflight, exact canonical source correspondence, source/discovery capacity, protected create-only publication, current-view refresh, correct new-retention/new-admission deltas, original occupied unique resolution and conservative publication uncertainty through final cleanup. Finish coherent composition and remove every fabrication-incomplete seam, temporary adapter, competing source path and obsolete helper. Only the resulting complete owner is eligible for the unchanged independent receiver and final source review. No production domain route, license selection, package release or completed assistant claim is introduced by these phases.


**F-S22 — Isolate existing-source synchronization from host repair.** Attempt21 supplied no B2b2 source. Generate B2b2a as the physical implementation of L-O28 and composition with the already reviewed requiredSourceClosure. It introduces a private reusable existing-file barrier and replaces requireDurableInScope; the two publication seams remain. This phase leaves all host initialization, gate, scanner and cleanup functions unchanged. B2b2b subsequently applies every F-S13 host correction using that same barrier, without claiming that B2b2a alone repairs the host or completes acceptance.

The private barrier accepts a bound absolute root, expected existing file descriptions and a caller-provided binding assertion. Descriptions identify root-relative nonsymlink regular files and their expected device/inode. Source and host descriptions also carry bounded exact previously verified bytes/digest and length; a stable maintenance-lock description can supply its already held descriptor without inventing semantic content or transferring descriptor ownership. It checks each named binding, reads bounded bytes from the verified descriptor, requires exact previous bytes/digest, and synchronizes selected physical files once while preserving all selected aliases for final checks. It holds and verifies the relevant ancestor directory descriptors before opening under them, synchronizes unique directories bottom-up through `/`, and rechecks named/held identities and caller bindings before success. Never create, publish, replace or delete anything. Close every descriptor it owns; preserve any primary thrown value using a separate failure flag, and surface a lone cleanup failure through the closed host diagnostic. Caller-owned descriptors remain open. The publication-uncertainty precedence still belongs to the protected outer operation and is completed in B2b2b/B2c.

requireDurableInScope invokes requiredSourceClosure, obtains the exact selected records from the current private view, runs that existing-source barrier, and stores the successful journal/semantic-reference/physical-source evidence privately behind a frozen opaque scope-bound receipt. It rechecks the live scope/bindings before acknowledgment. No serializable durable flag or public receipt validator is added. The private plan is never returned as proof of synchronization. Full L-O28 coverage and immutable independent receiving remain required after composition.

For this focused generation, supply exact excerpts containing the existing imports, required private helper definitions and the requireDurableInScope target, plus all top-level declaration names to prevent collisions. Bind each excerpt to its full file digest, original byte position and exact text; verify its occurrence before generation. The complete source file and ordinary F-P inventory stay bound and protected, and the unchanged materializer still resolves replacements against the entire file. Omit unrelated read-only dependency source and unrelated host-repair clauses from this invocation. This projection reduces input volume; it grants no authority to rewrite omitted code, extend the writable inventory or relax acceptance.

## L-O01 — Constructor and synchronous operation scope

The internal constructor is `openSourceOwner(storeDirectory)`, where storeDirectory is the explicit absolute physical journal directory obtained through L-H02's existing path laws. It validates/binds the root and host configuration but never initializes an absent store. Public `openJournal(root)` continues to take a settlement root; no second journal-directory suffix is added. Separate standalone stores retain their own admitted host configuration. Multiple owner objects referring to the same physical store use the same kernel gate and cannot execute concurrently, even within one process.

The owner exposes only `withOperation(perform)` to trusted System composition. It acquires the L-S04 gate, verifies root/lock/host identities, discovers and refreshes the complete bounded source view, invokes `perform(scope)` synchronously, checks identities again, constructs the result and releases its descriptor in a finally path. No user or model supplies perform. Detect a Promise/thenable return and refuse; never allow asynchronous host mutation to outlive the gate. A callback exception does not imply rollback of an already published source. Publication-uncertain precedence applies once publication may have occurred. No exception path unlinks the lock.

A scope is privately branded, belongs to that owner and operation epoch, and expires before lock release. Every method checks that lifetime. Retained scope objects, callbacks attempting a public nested operation, cross-owner use and reconstructed JSON objects cannot acquire authority; reentrant public access returns maintenance-busy. Pure immutable results may survive the scope; source handles, descriptors and durability evidence do not become reusable grants. Domain validation inside an operation receives this same scope and must not call a facade that reacquires the gate.


## L-O03 — Publication and readiness

The scope's `publishRetained(entries)` accepts only verified L-S01 entries from trusted journal construction or maintenance. Arbitrary remote requests cannot submit obstruction entries. Canonicalize with the existing codec, sort/deduplicate exact entries, enforce configured bounds, compute the exact complete-batch digest and use the accepted create-only durable helper. A nonempty valid batch is the publication unit; do not silently split an oversized batch or drop a witness to fit a budget. A domain may explicitly construct several bounded batches where its own atomicity/acknowledgment contract allows that.

Return internal `{disposition, digest, retainedEvents, admittedEvents}` with disposition `created` or `existing`, and ordinal unique event-reference arrays. `retainedEvents` means event identities newly given source custody by this operation; `admittedEvents` means identities newly entering the admitted state after refresh, including formerly pending events unlocked by the new source. Neither is inferred merely from batch creation. Adding a second feed membership to an already known event changes membership without pretending the event itself is newly retained/admitted. Adapters preserve their existing result's feed-specific meaning using the before/after view; do not equate these root-wide deltas with every facade's `written` count.

After publication refresh the same protected view to its bounded fixed point. No persistent admitted/pending/dependent index is written as authority. A pending source is durably retained but is not a successful causal admission. New source discovery must be visible to the next operation without restart/cache deletion; removed/changed immutable sources cannot be hidden by a warm cache. Cache only verified immutable values keyed by exact digest and physical identity, and reverify required closure bytes for acknowledgment.


## L-O05 — Registered unique domains and authority under protection

Unique admission is a trusted domain capability layered on this owner, not a general public `appendUnique` route. At host construction, bind an immutable domain registration naming `interaction` or `effect-successor`, its exact pure command validator, authenticated-principal source and protected-view new/occupied authority checks. The registration is an in-process capability kept by the Systems/domain composition; requests cannot select a validator, replace callbacks or supply an approved verdict. Do not infer production admission from a fixture registration.

The domain entry first validates canonical command identity and its trusted caller/context association, then enters this owner's operation. Resolve current authority against the supplied protected view; no asynchronous inference or network authorization is performed while holding the gate. The occupied path separately authorizes resolution before returning any reference, verifies the original record with `parseUniqueJournalRecord`, completes its closure barrier and returns existing/conflict by exact canonical-command correspondence. A denied resolver receives no occupied identity. A missing slot is an internal observation used only by the admitted creation path.

For a vacant slot, the registered new-transition check proves the exact predecessor/assignment/proposal/authority conditions required by its domain. Construct through `addressUniqueJournalCommand` and `uniqueJournalRecord`, barrier the necessary predecessor/artifacts, publish create-only, refresh, barrier the full retained closure and return created only to the live successful publisher. Unexpected occupancy despite exclusion takes the verified occupied path and never returns created. Keep public storage outcomes exactly L-J06's four variants and seven reasons. Domain refusal remains the domain's invalid/forbidden result before any source mutation; it is not a new storage-unavailable reason. The adapter must preserve this distinction rather than flattening every exception into an absent slot.

The protected scope supplies `uniqueRecord(slotDigest)` and `publishUnique(record)` solely to this trusted composition. `uniqueRecord` validates the digest, reads the authoritative slot, and returns null only for verified absence; otherwise it returns the deeply immutable exact parsed `{record, command, slotDigest, reference}` from `parseUniqueJournalRecord`. It neither checks a caller's domain authority nor grants publication authority. `publishUnique` validates the full candidate with the configured journal and computed slot digest, publishes canonical JSON plus one LF create-only under the same gate, refreshes the shared view, and returns exactly `{disposition, entry}`. Disposition is created only for this live successful publication, or existing when verified occupancy already exists; entry is the parsed authoritative record in either case. Existing occupancy never overwrites or echoes the proposed command as the retained one. This is an internal source-custody result, not a successful domain admission: the adapter must still perform the specified occupied authorization/command comparison and original-closure barrier. Any failure after possible publication uses publication-uncertain. These methods add no public route and cannot be invoked outside the branded live scope.

The concrete interaction and effect validators remain derived from their respective LLDs. Registration shape does not establish their correctness. Production unique dispatch stays unmounted until their source contracts and independent observations are accepted; a fixture may exercise storage with clearly labeled fixture authority.


## L-O14 — Facade folds preserve failure distinctions

The current scanCausalEvents catches both row decoding and the caller's fold in one catch, counting either failure as a malformed row. An isolated execution of the exact current function confirms a thrown application callback error becomes a successful-looking `{result:initial,rows:0,malformed:1}`. This is source migration evidence; it does not demonstrate a production occurrence.

In the replacement, verify the complete selected admitted source view before any fold callback, as L-O02 requires. Decode/classify each row separately from callback execution. A structurally valid non-row witness can contribute the documented non-row/malformed count without becoming an EAVT assertion. A recognized corrupt source or incomplete selected admission cannot be classified as an ignorable malformed row. Once a decoded row is passed to the caller, any callback-thrown value propagates unchanged; it must not increment malformed, return an empty result or appear to be a completed fold. Successful rows count completed callback applications. A thrown fold does not imply rollback of earlier in-memory accumulator mutations or published effects.

Apply the same distinction to feed, date, territory, subject and through-date folds, including trusted feed-selection predicates. Preserve their selected membership, causal ordering and result metadata while removing per-feed read-through authorities. Selection/fold callbacks remain synchronous and scoped; a thenable result refuses rather than escaping the protected operation. This does not make arbitrary callback code transactionally reversible or safe to run with broad host authority. Domain readers receive only the already admitted scope they need.

Receiving must show no callback runs on an incomplete selected feed, a valid decoded row reaches the callback exactly as before, a callback failure survives by identity/value, a genuine non-row witness is separately counted, and current work/authority readers cannot convert journal-unavailable into an empty successful history. The pure semantic-record resolver's separate exception-presence handling is the same required distinction, not a license to reuse application exception objects as an admission verdict.


## L-O22 — Historical blocking in the Code reconstruction law

Derive this refinement from L-S01's retained decisions and L-S05's common source-derived state. The current `rebuildCausalSubstrate(sources, site, causalEnvelope)` reconstructs from artifact bodies alone. It has no retained-decision input, so an otherwise complete cause and its descendant become admitted even when a separate retained record blocks the cause. Preserve that decision and the resulting blocked dependency closure in Code; Systems must not implement a second causal algorithm or promote first and delete admitted results afterward.

Extend that existing function with the optional fourth argument `retainedObstructions = []`. Its input is a finite array of exact `{event, obstruction}` records obtained from verified L-S01 retained-obstruction entries by trusted host composition. Event obeys the existing artifact-reference law. Obstruction is the original JSON value, including null, false, numbers, strings, arrays or objects; it is not required to have the current causal-obstruction schema. Validate and snapshot each entry with the existing bounded JSON codec, without invoking accessors or toJSON. Validate the array as an ordinary dense array of own data entries without serializing the whole collection through one artifact envelope. Each entry obeys the existing JSON resource envelope; aggregate retained-source and scan bounds remain the host's L-S03 obligation. Reject malformed input through `causalObstruction("retained-obstruction-invalid", "$.retainedObstructions", "retained obstruction input is invalid")`, without echoing private content. All validation precedes exposure or source reception by a new substrate.

Install the complete retained blocking set before the first promotion pass. Every event named by a retained decision has state blocked, including when its witness body is absent. Missing body does not manufacture a core, artifact, feed membership or admitted event. A later `receive` or `receiveSourceSet` can supply that body but cannot quarantine or admit the blocked reference. A descendant with such a cause is blocked by the existing cause-blocked rule, even if the cause body has not arrived. A retained decision cannot be superseded by ordinary artifacts, later source discovery, source enumeration order or a complete dependency closure. Existing three-argument calls retain their previous behavior.

Keep exact historical decisions separately from derived causal obstructions. Add `retainedObstructions()` returning a deeply immutable array of the exact `{event, obstruction}` snapshots, sorted by ordinal event reference and then ordinal canonical decision text, with only exact canonical duplicates removed. Also include this array under `retainedObstructions` in `snapshot()` so a caller preserving reconstruction inputs does not discard it. Multiple different decisions for one event all survive; no last-file-wins rule applies. `obstruction(event)` for a historically blocked event returns the fixed derived judgment `causalObstruction("retained-block", "$", "a retained journal admission decision blocks this witness", [event])`; the original decision is available through retainedObstructions and is not replaced by that explanation. Existing structurally derived obstruction behavior remains for other events. The snapshot's blocked array includes historically blocked references whose cores are absent, while witnesses lists only actual verified cores.

Every refreshed logical view must equal reconstruction from the complete current retained input set, including all retained decisions before computing readiness. L-O25 permits disposable derived-view reuse under exact source-set conditions; it does not omit historical decisions or introduce a second causal evaluator. Reuse of verified immutable bodies is allowed under L-S05; it does not permit omission of a retained decision. This contract does not add a mutable block/unblock API or admit arbitrary model/remote decisions. Historical affirmative admission evidence contradictory to a retained block is a source conflict to be reported under L-S01; an ordinary retained-witness record is only custody and is not such affirmative evidence. A unique occupied record whose required event is blocked cannot yield successful resolution or a replacement command; preserve the occupancy and return the applicable unavailable diagnostic.

Independent receiving must observe the same blocked cause and descendant across source permutations, exact duplicate and differing retained decisions, an absent blocked body later arriving, unrelated eligible witnesses, a missing unrelated dependency later arriving, and a reconstruction round trip carrying both sourceArtifacts and retainedObstructions. It must preserve falsy historical decisions and refuse malformed retained input without exposing a partial new view. These are pure state effects; accepting the codemod does not accept storage durability, migration, domain authority or the assistant workflow.


## L-O23 — Retained containers use the line capacity, not the artifact envelope

Derive this refinement from L-S01's preservation of original witness/decision values and independently verified canonical artifact text, L-S03/L-H03's pre-parse line bound, and L-O02's distinction between a document body and one string inside that document. The retained wrapper is a transport container, not an additional artifact with a new content identity. A valid composite artifact can encode to more than JSON_RESOURCE_ENVELOPE.maxStringBytes while each of its actual strings and its complete body remain within the artifact envelope. Refusing that body's retained wrapper under the artifact string bound loses a valid capability.

For one retained entry let B = configured maxLineBytes minus the one required LF. Before parsing, bound the complete physical line including LF; before publication, bound its canonical representation including LF. Admit/canonicalize the entry through the existing shared JSON codec with all eight envelope fields equal to B: maxSourceBytes, maxCanonicalBytes, maxDepth, maxNodes, maxObjectMembers, maxArrayLength, maxStringBytes and maxKeyBytes. No field is Infinity and no multiplication can overflow a safe integer. If B is zero, no nonempty entry can fit: return resource-limit without source mutation. These bounds admit every finite JSON structure whose canonical retained entry fits in the selected line capacity; an encoded node, nesting level, member, element, decoded string byte or key byte cannot require fewer than its counted JSON bytes. This is a transport capacity derived from the already explicit host limit, not a replacement artifact codec or an extra hidden depth limit.

After strict transport admission, verify the closed retained-entry shape and its field laws. Verify each artifact body with the existing artifact verifier and unchanged JSON_RESOURCE_ENVELOPE. Verify every ordinary witness with parseJournalWitness, retaining the original verified value separately from its normalized result; original permitted fields and source order must survive. Validate retained decisions under L-O22's per-decision envelope. The larger wrapper envelope grants none of these inner values a larger semantic envelope. Unique-slot records retain L-S02/L-J01's fixed whole-record envelope, not this wrapper envelope. Host configuration retains its separate exact byte limit. A parsed object or a fit within the byte budget alone proves neither identity nor admissibility.

The shared codec's strict text parser and runtime canonical projection must traverse finite JSON using explicit work frames rather than JavaScript call-stack recursion. Preserve RFC 8785 text, UTF-8 measurements, frozen snapshots, duplicate-key/Unicode/number rejection, descriptor safety, cycle detection, the default envelopes and all eight limit meanings. Keep path ancestry as linked segments until a diagnostic needs its path; accumulate output once rather than rebuilding the full serialization at each ancestor. Deep admissible values must not fail with RangeError merely because they are deeply nested. A configured depth/node/byte limit must be charged and refused by its existing typed diagnostic. The existing raw isJsonValue predicate used by requireJsonValue/parseJournalWitness must likewise traverse iteratively while preserving its distinct existing raw-JSON semantics and cycle/shared-subtree behavior. Do not add an alternate parser in Systems or weaken the artifact verifier to work around a codec limit.

The diagnostic boundary remains L-M09: oversize physical custody or an over-capacity proposed batch is resource-limit; malformed recognized custody is source-corrupt. A JavaScript stack overflow is a fabrication defect, not an accepted resource-limit observation. No truncation, dropped unknown observation field or alternate content address repairs the failure. The owner must bound input before invoking the codec and still enforce total batch/source/scan budgets; the codec does not supply filesystem bounds.

Receiving must demonstrate a valid multi-field artifact whose encoded body exceeds the individual-string limit can round-trip through a fitting retained wrapper while an actually invalid inner artifact is still refused. Observe deep finite retained metadata within capacity, deliberate depth refusal, shared subtrees versus cycles, strict malformed/duplicate/Unicode rejection and unchanged canonical identities for prior ordinary values. Acceptance of these pure codec effects alone does not establish owner integration, durable custody or assistant operation.


## L-O25 — Source-derived reuse without a second causal evaluator

L-S05 requires warm ordinary admission not to reverify the entire unrelated history. L-O22 requires every refreshed logical view to include all current historical decisions before readiness is judged. Satisfy both with a disposable derived view in the owner. Complete bounded discovery still occurs under every protected operation. Read and hash recognized bounded source bytes and compare their exact identities/digests before using cached parsed records. A warm cache never suppresses new, missing, changed or malformed source evidence and never enlarges the configured source/scan budgets.

If the complete verified source and decision sets are unchanged, reuse the immutable parsed records and existing causal substrate. For monotone additions with an unchanged historical-decision set, verify newly discovered source records, retain all feed memberships, and deliver only previously unseen verified artifact source pairs through the existing substrate's receiveSourceSet. Preserve new pending bodies so a later missing dependency triggers the existing fixed point. The substrate alone computes causal state; Systems must not mutate its internal admitted/blocked maps or copy those maps into a new object as an alternative evaluator. Adding a feed membership for an existing witness is a membership change even when no new semantic source is delivered.

On source withdrawal, replacement of an admitted physical binding, changed historical decisions, or an invalidated derived view, discard the affected cached judgment and rebuild from the complete current verified source/decision inputs through rebuildCausalSubstrate. A malformed or identity-conflicting current source refuses rather than becoming an implicit removal. Install all current retained blocking decisions before the reconstruction's first promotion pass. Required acknowledged closure bytes are reread and synchronized under L-O04 even on cache hits. A changed host/root binding still ends the owner lifetime under L-H02; a source refresh cannot follow it into another store.

Thus 'reconstruct from current sources' is a provenance requirement, not an instruction to replay unrelated verification on every ordinary append. Reuse is allowed only when it is equivalent to cold reconstruction of the exact current sources and retained decisions. No persistent index, hidden recovery flag or writable cache file is introduced. Receiving must observe cold/warm equivalence, unchanged-history verification reuse, late dependency recovery, membership-only additions, newly discovered blocks and source withdrawal/alteration; private instrumentation may establish avoided verification without adding production counters or telemetry APIs.


## L-O26 — Command-body custody in a unique source

Derive this correspondence from L-J05's complete retained command, L-S02's shared source resolver, and L-O05's original occupied reference. `parseUniqueJournalRecord` returns a verified command and a reference whose payload is the command's artifact address. The command is embedded in the authoritative record; the wire format does not also list its body among `record.artifacts` or the witness's six source pairs. Discovery must therefore address the parsed command with the existing `addressArtifact`, require that address to equal both `record.commandRef` and `reference.payload`, and register its canonical body with custody in that exact unique-slot source. Deliver this verified pair to the same causal substrate as the record's other source pairs. No new addressing law, artifact file, retained entry or redundant command field is needed.

`artifact(reference.payload)` resolves that pair under the live protected scope. The resolution still requires an admitted, verified source; an arbitrary JSON subvalue whose content happens to be addressable is not automatically registered. This rule applies specifically to the command already verified by the unique-record parser. Conflicting bodies for any one artifact reference are source-corrupt, not last-file-wins. An ordinary copy of the command body may supply artifact custody but never occupancy. Removing the unique source removes that occupancy and its custody contribution on the next refresh; another verified body source can still supply artifact resolution.

When `requireDurable` includes a uniqueSlot, include the parsed original command's artifact reference explicitly, as well as the original witness and its closure. The authoritative slot file is mandatory custody even if another file contains an equivalent command or witness. Refuse a missing slot rather than reconstructing it from those copies. On a conflicting proposed command, resolve and barrier the occupied command's body, never the proposal. Charge the command body once in the artifact-reference set even if several required records reference it. The existing whole-record and inner artifact limits remain in force.

Independent receiving must reopen from only the authoritative unique source and resolve the returned payload to the exact original command, with no auxiliary artifact file. Observe an occupied conflicting proposal, copied ordinary bodies without occupancy, source withdrawal, malformed correspondence and a barrier containing the original payload even when the explicit artifact argument is empty. The accompanying current-law observation establishes the missing listed pair and the existing parser/address correspondence only; it does not establish an owner implementation.

**L-S01 — Ordinary retained entries.** The new source namespace is `retained/v1/<digest>.jsonl` under the owning journal directory. Digest is lowercase SHA-256 of the exact complete file bytes. It is an internal container locator, not an artifact reference or a grant. A file contains one or more canonical-JSON entries, each followed by exactly one LF. Sort entries by ordinal comparison of their canonical JSON text and omit exact duplicate entries within a batch. Empty lines, noncanonical JSON, a missing final LF and a filename/body digest mismatch are corruption. New batches are immutable and published create-only through the accepted durable filesystem helper. Staging files are outside the recognized source namespace.

An entry is exactly one of:

- `{kind:"metroplat.journal.retained-witness",version:1,feed,statement}`. Statement satisfies the existing ordinary journal-witness verifier. Feed is the exact root-relative ordinary feed locator: nonempty, slash-separated, no empty/dot/dot-dot components, no NUL, backslash, absolute prefix or root escape. Resolve it inside the configured journal root. Feed membership is custody metadata; it does not change the witness ID. The same witness can belong to several feeds; preserve every distinct pair. Retain the original verified statement value, including historical source-array order; use the verifier's normalized value for comparison and judgment. Do not silently discard original observation fields during migration.
- `{kind:"metroplat.journal.retained-artifact",version:1,ref,canonicalText}`. Verify the existing artifact address and require byte-equal canonical text. This retains bodies currently held only by `artifacts.jsonl` or legacy object files. It is independent source custody, not a derived lookup.
- `{kind:"metroplat.journal.retained-obstruction",version:1,event,obstruction}`. Event is an existing valid content reference; obstruction is the exact retained JSON decision from the old blocked source or a decision produced by the trusted causal admission boundary. It is an attributable journal admission decision, not a personal authorization or a model's truth assertion. Remote append input cannot supply arbitrary obstruction entries. Preserve historical obstruction evidence even where the associated witness body is unavailable; do not invent a missing witness.

No entry carries a mutable admitted flag, missing-dependency list, repeated command reference, or independently editable copy of a witness's time/subject. Future states are reconstructed. A historical blocked decision remains a blocking input until a separately specified attributable superseding decision exists; this order does not reinterpret it as a newly admitted event merely because a current lookup lacks it. Contradictory retained admitted/blocked evidence must be reported, not silently resolved by file ordering.


**L-S02 — Unique records and shared custody.** L-J05's `unique-admissions/v1/<slotDigest>.json` remains the only source of unique-slot occupancy. Read its exact canonical record plus LF and verify the slot, configured journal and complete record through the accepted pure functions. Every verified unique witness participates in ordinary causal/artifact discovery as well. Its artifacts are source bodies and its witness sources are available to the same resolver. A copied witness in an ordinary batch preserves history but never proves occupancy or grants created status. Query deduplication is by verified event ID; ordinary membership is additionally keyed by feed.

For discovery, a unique event has a virtual feed constructed by the existing journal feed-address law using its original verified time, subject, and the action `metroplat.journal.unique-admission`. No physical dated projection is required. Date and subject filtering for unique events use those verified values. Exact unique resolution always reads the authoritative slot, including after an ordinary projection exists.


**L-S03 — Capacity, source admission and corruption.** All source reads are bounded before JSON parsing. The host storage profile supplies positive integer capacities for line bytes, batch bytes, source-file count, aggregate scan bytes, closure witness/artifact count, closure bytes and traversal depth. The fabrication order must pin the initial profile and show it admits the migration corpus and required acceptance fixtures. These are host capacity limits, not changes to the fixed v1 command/envelope limits in L-J01. Exceeding a host capacity returns explicit resource-limit; it neither changes a wire identity nor licenses truncation, omission or deletion. An ordinary historical source beyond the current capacity remains retained and unavailable until an adequate admitted profile is supplied.

Read errors other than a verified absence refuse as unavailable. A malformed recognized source is source-corrupt, never an empty feed or an ignored line. Recovering an interrupted old append file requires explicit migration treatment; runtime must not trim an unverified tail and pretend the source is complete. Refusals expose the L-J06 closed reason vocabulary and retain private diagnostics separately from public responses.

## One host operation boundary


**L-S04 — System-owned exclusion.** All source writes, source-dependent reads, unique admission, recovery and migration for one journal root use the same System-owned exclusive operation gate. The admitted initial host mechanism is a local Linux kernel flock held by the owning journal process's open file description. Use a stable `maintenance.lock` inode under the owning journal root; never unlink it to release or reclaim it. Bind the root and lock to their verified device/inode identities. Reject unexpected symlink/nonregular lock targets and a changed root binding.

The acquiring helper is short-lived: the owner opens the lock descriptor and passes it explicitly as child fd 3 to a noninteractive `flock --exclusive --nonblock 3` invocation. The helper exits after acquisition; the owner keeps its descriptor open until the operation finishes. A contention exit maps to maintenance-busy. Unsupported mechanism or storage semantics maps to storage-unsupported. Other host errors map to storage-unavailable. Closing the owner's descriptor releases protection; no stale PID lookup, lease expiration or lock-file removal is involved. A separate long-lived helper is not allowed to be the only lock holder while an unprotected parent continues work.

The mechanism has been observed on this host in both Python and the actual Node runtime; see the [descriptor ownership observations](evidence/2026-09-27-journal-maintenance-lock/README.md). Those observations do not admit other filesystem types or deployment environments. Fabrication acceptance must exercise the actual System gate, in-process contention, separate processes, owner death and unsupported-host refusal. A process-local mutex alone is insufficient.

Hold the gate across discovery, exact-byte verification, causal judgment, required-source synchronization, unique publication and result construction. Public storage operations enter once. Internal readers receive the existing protected source view; they do not reacquire the lock. Reentrant public calls refuse rather than deadlock or silently run outside protection. Host mutation must remain synchronous inside the selected initial gate; no unresolved Promise can outlive it. Authenticate upstream before entering, then perform state-dependent domain checks against this protected view. No model or remote caller selects a validator, journal root or lock path.

An advisory gate constrains only compliant writers. Migration requires admitted evidence that old writers are quiescent and every replacement writer uses the gate. It must not run destructive cleanup against a live old process merely because that process does not know the new lock. A working checkout containing the new code is not evidence of deployment-wide exclusion.

## Recovery and read effects


**L-S05 — Source-derived state.** On opening a root, discover the complete recognized source set under protection and verify its sources. Build maps for event identity, feed membership, artifact custody, historical blocking evidence and reverse causal dependencies. Reuse the existing Code causal laws to derive admitted, quarantined and blocked states. A retained but not ready witness is not returned as admitted. Pending evidence must become eligible when its missing cause/artifact is later retained, without a manual cache deletion or restart.

The ordinary append path verifies and durably publishes a batch containing new witnesses and supplied artifact bodies, then updates the protected source view and computes readiness. It does not append a second admitted index record or copy a pending witness into another authority when readiness changes. The result distinguishes newly retained source from newly admitted witness; preserve the observable meaning of existing `written`/`appended` results as newly admitted witnesses when adapting current consumers. Internal source publication receipts must not be exposed as proof that a pending witness was admitted.

Every operation enumerates the two recognized source namespaces before relying on cached discovery. Cache immutable verified entries by source filename/digest and stable file identity; invalidate on new, removed or changed source. A dated-directory timestamp cannot summarize the flat unique namespace. A warm operation may reuse verified unrelated immutable source entries but must re-open and verify the exact requested/required closure before acknowledging its durability. A cold open may need one bounded scan; repeated admissions must not re-verify unrelated historical artifact bodies. The scanner must report capacity or I/O failure explicitly instead of hiding undiscovered sources behind a valid partial view.

There is no persistent admitted lookup to repair in the final runtime. An old source/index publication gap is resolved by importing the actual witness source; the old admitted lookup cannot veto it. Do not treat an old segment's existence alone as causal proof: verify its witness and its required causal/artifact closure. Cycles, missing bodies, conflicting representations and structurally blocked causes remain explicit obstructions. Reconstruct readiness to a fixed point with bounded work; never truncate a required dependency chain and call it admitted.


**L-S07 — Required closure barrier.** Starting from the candidate or occupied unique record, traverse its full required witness/artifact closure under the gate. Each resolved reference records the verified source file(s) containing its exact bytes. Deduplicate shared physical files; retain all semantic references in the internal barrier evidence. Synchronize every required source descriptor and directory entries bottom-up through the filesystem root as L-J07 requires. A verified root initialization barrier may discharge ancestors only under that exact unchanged root binding. A cache hit, inode existence or another closure's receipt is insufficient.

The internal successful evidence contains the configured journal identity, the sorted verified event/artifact references and the protected source content digests. It is returned only after every required synchronization succeeds. It grants no external dispatch permission and exposes no filesystem path in a public result. No closure file may be removed or replaced between verification and acknowledgment. Failure yields the L-J06 unavailable reason and retains already published bytes; it does not assert rollback.

## Necessary transformation

L-F02's exact-substring contract cannot create a System module or retire its superseded Code implementation. L-S06/L-S09 require both effects, including consumer migration. This order extends the deterministic materialization boundary for explicitly declared source creation and deletion. It does not add a scheduler, model harness, repository mutation service or product-code generator. Existing edit-only orders and their evidence remain unchanged. The source provider continues deriving behavioral source; the operator's deterministic materializer performs only declared byte transformations on a fresh staged directory.

**F-P01 — Opt-in input.** A patchset work order binds an exact source root and an input inventory. The inventory is a JSON object with exactly `kind`, `version`, `sourceRoot`, `files`, `clauses`. Kind is `source-patchset-input`; version is integer 1. SourceRoot is an absolute existing directory. Files is a path-keyed object. Every key is an admitted relative POSIX source path: nonempty components, each matching `[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+`, no dot/dot-dot component, absolute prefix, backslash or NUL. Each descriptor is exactly either `{state:"present",sha256}` or `{state:"absent"}`. Present entries bind lowercase SHA-256 of original bytes; absent entries authorize only creation. No path may be an ancestor of another admitted path. Clauses is a nonempty unique list of recognized nonempty clause-ID strings. Existing paths must be ordinary regular files and all existing ancestors, including the root's own path, must be nonsymlink directories; absent paths must also have no symlink or nondirectory ancestor. The inventory is trusted work-order input, not generated permission to touch files.

The concrete storage order must enumerate its exact writable files and clause IDs before source generation. This generic extension grants no writable source path by itself. Read-only dependencies and governing specification hashes remain protected under L-F01/L-F07 and are additional to this writable inventory.

**F-P02 — Closed candidate.** The new opt-in output is exactly `{kind:"source-patchset",version:1,disposition,reason,changes}`. Disposition is `candidate` or `refused`; reason is a string. A refusal has zero changes. A candidate has at least one change. Each admitted path occurs at most once, and every change contains a nonempty unique `clauses` array drawn from the inventory. No generated shell command, URL, dependency installation, permission change or recursive delete operation exists.

Changes are exactly one of:

- `{operation:"edit",path,inputSha256,replacements,clauses}` against a present entry. Each replacement is exactly `{before,after}`. Before is nonempty text occurring exactly once when that replacement is applied; after is text. Apply replacements in order against the original bound UTF-8 text. The one input digest remains the original file digest, not an intermediate value. The list is nonempty.
- `{operation:"create",path,text,clauses}` against an absent entry. Text is complete strict UTF-8 source, supplied by the generator; the operator must not fill behavioral placeholders. Creation emits an ordinary file with mode 0644. An executable entrypoint should normally be invoked through its existing runtime; changing execution bits requires a separately admitted order.
- `{operation:"delete",path,inputSha256,clauses}` against a present entry. This removes that exact file from the staged result. It does not delete directories, follow links, delete imports automatically or authorize removing unlisted data. Necessary consumer and export changes must appear as separately bound changes in the same work family.

All objects are closed. Reject Boolean values masquerading as integer versions, unknown operations, malformed digests, repeated paths, unknown clauses, invalid UTF-8, missing inputs, changed input bytes or an unexpectedly present creation target. Do not normalize generated paths or repair a refused candidate.

**F-P03 — Validate before staging.** The materializer rechecks every inventory entry, including unchanged inputs, before creating any staged output. It validates the whole candidate and calculates all intended output bytes in memory before writing. A malformed candidate therefore leaves no stage directory. It may inspect file metadata and bytes, but it never imports, evaluates or executes candidate text. The only mechanical transformations are the specified text replacements, creation and file omission.

Use a fresh nonexistent stage directory outside the source root. A stage ancestor cannot be a symlink or non-directory. The operator chooses that path; it is not accepted from the candidate. Copy each unchanged admitted present file and each resulting changed file into the stage at its declared relative path, preserving the existing file's permission bits for retained/edited files. Deleted inputs are omitted and their digests/modes retained in the receipt. Do not copy the repository's unbounded contents or leave links from the stage into the working checkout. Recheck all original inputs after staging before writing the staged result receipt. A concurrent change invalidates the stage and prevents acceptance; it does not authorize changing the concurrent work.

A host I/O error during staging may leave a partial staged directory. It must have no successful receipt; report failure and preserve it for inspection. Do not represent staging as an atomic multi-file filesystem transaction. A retry uses a fresh stage and fresh validation rather than overwriting an uncertain directory.

**F-P04 — Staged receipt and assessment.** The operator writes a sibling `<stage>.receipt.json` only after successful validation/staging/revalidation. The receipt contains kind `source-patchset-stage`, integer version 1, inventory/candidate digests, the materializer digest, each original path's presence/digest/mode, each final path's presence/digest/mode, and disposition `staged-unaccepted`. No receipt claims product acceptance or promotion. A receipt target already present refuses before staging; receipt creation is exclusive. A receipt write failure is a failed stage operation even if all source files have been written.

Independent assessment uses the exact staged tree plus explicitly admitted read-only dependencies. A retired file must be absent from that assessment namespace; a fallback mount of the old checkout must not make deleted code available again. Verify source creation, changed consumers and actual retired routes, not only that new files load. The private assessment remains excluded from source generation under L-F03–L-F05. Source provider and materializer receive no permission to amend acceptance fixtures after a failure.

**F-P05 — Promotion remains separate.** This materializer has no shared-checkout mutation or deployment mode. Product promotion remains governed by L-F07 plus the concrete work order's creation/deletion preconditions. Recheck all present/absent expectations before touching any target. Do not delete an obsolete file unless the complete affected capability and consumer migration have independently passed. A staged tree, deleted-path list or model assertion is insufficient. A multi-file promotion must record partial host failure accurately; it must not claim atomicity that the filesystem mechanism does not provide. Never restore over unrelated concurrent edits while trying to roll back a partial operation.

**F-P06 — Independent mechanical observations.** Demonstrate in disposable files that one batch creates a new file, changes an exact unique substring, retires a bound old file and carries an unchanged input, while leaving the source root byte-identical. Exercise stale/absent mismatch, ambiguous replacement, malformed/extra fields, repeated changes, unknown clause, path traversal, symlink input/ancestor, a path ancestor collision, malformed UTF-8 and an existing stage/receipt. Invalid input must produce no successful receipt or shared source mutation. The observations verify deterministic materialization only; they do not accept any journal or assistant behavior.

The initial realization may be a small operator-owned script retained with the fabrication evidence and invoked directly. It is not a new runtime package. This is mechanical tooling under the closed contract above; all product behavioral text in real candidates must still originate from the admitted isolated source-generation process.
